description: CAD bake-off 1 of 3 -- OPENSCAD: build the SO-101 gripper assembly parametrically in cad/openscad/. SHARED CONTEXT (same task, three tools, one pebble each so they can run in separate git worktrees): recreate the SO-101 gripper assembly -- the fixed jaw (gripper body) and the moving jaw -- as a baseline for comparing three CAD tools. Jake verbatim: "I want to be able to modify them in the future, so you will have to do it in a way that supports that." That means parametric, editable source. Importing a mesh and calling it done FAILS the test. Use named variables for every dimension that might plausibly change: jaw length, jaw opening, fingertip thickness, servo horn bore, fastener sizes, wall thickness. DIMENSIONAL SOURCE OF TRUTH -- two real SO-101 STEP files are already committed at cad/build123d/reference/: Moving_Jaw_SO101.step and Wrist_Roll_Follower_SO101.step. STEP carries exact analytic geometry, so measure from these. Do NOT re-download them and do NOT invent or eyeball dimensions from tessellated meshes. WHY THIS PART: it is what Jake will modify for the Hand 1.0 paper gripper -- cross-reference plans/hand_1_0.md and plans/gripper_bet.md as reading, and cite them in your notes. DELIVERABLE BESIDES THE MODEL: a NOTES.md in your own tool directory covering time taken, what was easy, what was painful, whether the tool known weakness actually mattered in practice, and how it would feel to modify this part six months from now. State plainly if the geometry ends up approximate and list what still needs verifying. BOUNDARIES: stay inside your own cad/<tool>/ directory and touch nothing else. Do NOT edit plans/hand_1_0.md or plans/gripper_bet.md -- a later pass writes the comparison across all three tools. The other two tool pebbles are running in parallel in their own worktrees, so do not touch cad/openscad/, cad/build123d/, or cad/blender/ other than your own. TOOL SPECIFICS: OpenSCAD is installed at /Applications/OpenSCAD.app; the CLI binary is inside the bundle at /Applications/OpenSCAD.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenSCAD. Write .scad source with a named-variable block at the top. Prove it compiles by rendering a PNG and exporting an STL from the CLI, both committed. Note the reference STEP files live under cad/build123d/reference/ -- read them for dimensions only (OpenSCAD cannot import STEP, so measure and transcribe), and write nothing into that directory. KNOWN LIMITATION TO EVALUATE HONESTLY IN NOTES.md: OpenSCAD is mesh output only -- no B-rep, no true fillets, no STEP export. Does that actually bite on THIS part, or is it irrelevant here? Give a real verdict, not a hedge. The upside to weigh against it: a single self-contained file with no dependencies.
test_instructions: cad/openscad/ contains parametric .scad source with a named-variable block covering jaw length, jaw opening, fingertip thickness, servo horn bore, fastener sizes and wall thickness
A PNG render and an STL export produced by /Applications/OpenSCAD.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenSCAD are committed
cad/openscad/NOTES.md covers time, easy, painful, whether the no-B-rep/no-fillet/no-STEP limitation mattered on this part, six-month modifiability, and what still needs verifying
Nothing outside cad/openscad/ is modified -- in particular plans/hand_1_0.md and plans/gripper_bet.md are untouched

results.identified_issue:
Task: OpenSCAD leg of the three-tool CAD bake-off. Recreate the SO-101 gripper
assembly (Wrist_Roll_Follower = fixed jaw + servo cradle; Moving_Jaw) as
parametric, editable source, measured from the STEP files at
cad/build123d/reference/.

APPROACH AND WHY
OpenSCAD cannot import STEP, so the first job was building a measuring
instrument: cad/openscad/tools/measure_step.py parses the AP214 text with the
stdlib alone and prints every PLANE as signed-normal + offset and every
CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE as radius + axis + location, plus a bbox from VERTEX_POINTs
only (B-spline control points lie outside the solid and inflate a naive
min/max -- the moving jaw's naive Z range is +-455 mm, its real one is +-24).
I also used a throwaway OpenCascade (cadquery-ocp) script for face AREAS and
cross-SECTIONS, because "which of these forty planes is the big one" is a
question the text will not answer. That script survives, cleaned up, as
tools/compare_to_step.py; it is the only thing here with a dependency.

The model is a functional reconstruction, not a surface copy. Interfaces,
bolt patterns, blade profiles and envelopes are measured; the organic shell
corners are hulled rounded rectangles. Both blades are built by hulling
neighbouring cross-sections (common.scad loft_y / loft_z), which gets the taper
AND the stepped gripping faces from one mechanism -- a repeated station with
different values reads as a step rather than a blend.

THE ONE LOAD-BEARING INFERENCE
The two STEP files are separate solids in separate local frames; the export
carries no assembly transform. jaw_pivot_x = 4.4 and jaw_pivot_z = 23.375 were
SOLVED, not read. Evidence: with that transform the moving jaw's last gripping
step (face x=-12.3, spanning y -72..-82) coincides with the fixed jaw's last
step (face x=-7.9, spanning z 95.375..104.400) -- same plane, same 10 mm run,
and both fingertips land on z=105.375. Four numbers agreeing at once. It also
means jaw_opening=0 is the true closed pose with the pads touching. If a future
agent finds this wrong, everything else in params.scad still stands; only
gripper.scad's jaw_place() moves.

ALTERNATIVE REJECTED: I briefly considered a pivot near x=-26, which would have
put the moving jaw's fork around the follower's rear tower (walls at y=+-15.954,
x -32.2..-19.3 -- a tempting fit). Rejected because it puts the moving jaw's
gripping face at X=-34.3, behind the fixed jaw's face at -15..-7.9, i.e. on the
wrong side. Flipping the jaw's X to fix that flips its face normal too. Dead end.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY (also listed in NOTES.md section 6)
1. A real 1.3 mm slot at mid-height on the moving jaw's back face, ~11 mm deep,
   running most of the blade. Not an artifact (unlike the ~0.2 mm hairline split
   faces at 5 stations on the same blade, which ARE artifacts of the original
   modelling and are correctly ignored). I do not know its purpose; not modelled.
2. The cradle side walls come out 1.682 mm thick above fj_fork_clear_z, which
   falls out of a measured pocket half-width (16.0) and a measured boss face
   (17.682). That is thinner than a servo cradle should be, so one of those two
   is probably mis-identified. params.scad echoes the number on every compile.
3. fj_fork_clear_z = 14.0 is a guess -- the height at which the body steps in so
   the fork can sweep over it.
4. The gripper servo is not modelled. I never positively identified an
   STS3215-shaped cavity; the cradle is a C-section open toward +X that matches
   the cross-sections but is not proof.
5. jaw_opening_max = 55 is invented. At that angle the jaw hub clips the cable
   tab in render/gripper_open.png -- possibly a real limit, possibly a symptom of
   (3). Real travel is set by the servo (1594-3018 ticks per plans/hand_1_0.md).
6. Nothing printed or checked against the arm on the bench.

STILL MISSING: an interference assert. params.scad asserts fork-vs-boss width,
pad coincidence at closed, and step direction, but nothing checks that the jaws
stay clear of each other through the stroke. intersection() at several openings
should be empty; at jaw_opening_max it is not.

BOUNDARIES RESPECTED: only cad/openscad/ was written. plans/hand_1_0.md and
plans/gripper_bet.md are untouched (NOTES.md links them and argues with
hand_1_0.md section 6, but does not edit it). cad/build123d/ and cad/blender/
were read-only / not touched. The repo .gitignore has *.stl, so the required STL
exports are un-ignored by cad/openscad/export/.gitignore rather than by editing
the root file, which the other two worktrees also have open.
results.summary: Rebuilt the SO-101 gripper parametrically in OpenSCAD, measured off the reference STEP files, with the bake-off verdict in cad/openscad/NOTES.md.
results.detailed_description:
cad/openscad/ now has the SO-101 gripper as parametric source: params.scad holds every dimension as a named variable, and both jaws are built by hulling measured cross-sections, so editing a row of mj_blade_profile or mj_face_steps reshapes the blade. Open gripper.scad; set jaw_opening in millimetres and the jaw swings on the pivot.

Every dimension is tagged [STEP], [DERIVED] or [GUESS]. OpenSCAD cannot read STEP, so I wrote tools/measure_step.py to pull planes and cylinders straight out of the reference files with no dependencies. render/fidelity_check.png overlays the rebuild on the reference in three views so you can see where it drifts instead of taking my word for it.

The verdict you asked for, in NOTES.md: mesh-only output and the lack of true fillets never bit on this part, because its rounding is 2D swept along a blade and offset(r=) does that exactly. What cost me was the other direction — more than half the run went into reading a file format OpenSCAD cannot open. build123d would have started modelling 45 minutes of proportional time earlier.

Two things to know before trusting it. The assembly transform is solved, not measured — the STEP files carry no assembly, so I pinned the pivot by the fingertip pads landing on the same plane and the same 105.375 tip. And the cradle walls come out 1.68 mm thick above the fork line, which is thinner than it should be, so one of my pocket-width or fork-clearance numbers is off by a couple of millimetres. Calipers on the real arm settle it in thirty seconds. Five more open items are listed in NOTES.md §6.
